'''A Philosophical Essay on Probabilities''' is a work by [[Pierre-Simon Laplace]] on the mathematical [[theory of probability]].<ref name=wustl-a-philosophical-essay>{{Cite book|title=A Philosophical Essay on Probabilities|last=Laplace|first=Pierre-Simon|publisher=[[Wiley (publisher)|John Wiley & Son]] and [[Chapman & Hall]]|url=https://bayes.wustl.edu/Manual/laplace_A_philosophical_essay_on_probabilities.pdf|translator-last=Trruscott|translator-first=Frederick Wilson|translator-last2=Emory|translator-first2=Frederick Lincoln}}</ref><ref name=britannica-a-philosophical-essay>{{Cite web|url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Philosophical-Essay-on-Probabilities|title=Philosophical Essay on Probabilities - work by Laplace|access-date=2021-04-09|website=[[Encyclopædia Britannica]]}}</ref><ref name=figures-laplace>{{Cite web|url=http://www.economics.soton.ac.uk/staff/aldrich/Figures.htm#lap|title=Figures from the History of Probability and Statistics|access-date=2021-04-09|website=Figures from the History of Probability and Statistics}}</ref> The book consists of two parts, the first with five chapters and the second with thirteen.<ref name=wustl-a-philosophical-essay/>
==Table of Contents==
*Part I - A Philosophical Essay on Probabilities<ref name=wustl-a-philosophical-essay/>
#Introduction
#Concerning Probability
#General Principles of the Calculus of Probability
#Concerning Hope
#Analytical Methods of the Calculus of Probability
*Part II - Application of the Calculus of Probabilities<ref name=wustl-a-philosophical-essay/>
#Games of Chance
#Concerning the Unknown Inequalities which may Exist among Chances Supposed to be Equal
#Concerning the Laws of Probability which result from the Indefinite Multiplication of Events
#Application of the Calculus of Probabilities to Natural Philosophy
#Application of the Calculus of Probabilities to the Moral Sciences
#Concerning the Probability of Testimonies
#Concerning the Selections and Deliberations of Assemblies
#Concerning the Probability of the Judgements of Tribunals
#Concerning Tables of Mortality, and the Mean Durations of Life, Marriage and Some Assemblies
#Concerning the Benefits of Institutions which Depend on the Probability of Events
#Concerning Illusions in the Estimation of Probabilities
#Concerning the Various Means of Approaching Certainty
#Historical Note of the Calculus of Probabilities to 1816
